children: According to Sina Finance, Goldman Sachs spent more than a year working on a way for technology companies to buy AI chips without damaging their balance sheets. On Thursday, Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management presented a plan that helped SpaceX price $32 billion in bonds combining features of corporate debt and asset-backed securities. The financing is costly for SpaceX but could serve as a model for other technology companies buying chips.

Chips are expensive and have useful lives of only a few years. Companies making large purchases may avoid conventional corporate bonds because additional borrowing could increase their debt and lead to credit-rating downgrades. Asset-backed securities can fund purchases without adding debt that affects the issuer’s credit rating, but the market for these securities has limited capacity.

Chip purchasing demand is estimated at about $1.5 trillion over the coming period, with much of it expected to be debt-financed. The only credit market of comparable scale is the U.S. investment-grade corporate bond market, with about $8.3 trillion outstanding.

People familiar with the matter said Goldman Sachs proposed the structure to SpaceX this summer. A special-purpose vehicle would buy Nvidia chips and issue bonds, with repayments supported by a roughly five-year lease agreement with Musk’s rocket, satellite and AI company. The structure is essentially an asset-backed security.

The notes also share features with conventional corporate bonds, including CUSIP security identifiers, allowing them to be offered to investment-grade corporate bond investors. Buyers included insurers, structured-credit investors, asset managers and pension funds, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Goldman Sachs Designs SpaceX Financing Plan to Address AI Chip Debt Challenge
